units.translation: 322-23a. κορθύεται: the water, seething above them, penetrates through. στρηνές is that which is stretched taut, and great, and sharp, and piercing.
b. 〈κορθύεται βρασσόμενον:〉 it resounds. Sm
c. βρασσόμενον instead of 'being lifted with noise and disturbance'. P
d. στρηνές: hard. Lg P
e. στυφελή is the rugged shore. P
324. τῷ νῦν ἡμετέ〈ρῃσι〉: therefore now, since the danger is great and abundant. παραιφασίῃσι means exhortations, counsels.
325. ἀλέγειν instead of φροντίζειν (to care for). P
326a. πείρειν here means to sail through and cross over, as in 'ἀλεγεινά τε κύματα πείρων' (Hom.), but elsewhere it means to pierce through: 'σπλάγχνα δ’ ἄρ’ ἀμπείραντες' (B 426). P
b. αὐτάγρετον: self-chosen. Lg P
327. θύνειν means to rush. Those who write ἰθύνειν are mistaken. P

328-29a. οἰωνῷ δὴ πρό〈σθε〉: the order is: οἰωνῷ δὴ πρόσθε πελειάδι πειρήσεσθε ἐφιέμενοι. πελειάς is a kind of dove, as Aristotle (Hist. an. V 13, 544 b 1) says. That they used a dove when about to sail, Asclepiades also says in his Tragodoumenoi (12 fg 2 b J.).

b. πρόσθε indicates 'before', and ἀποπρό 'far away'. ἐφιέναι here means to send forth, but sometimes it means to command and entrust; among the orators it specifically means to transfer from one court to another, and ἔφεσις is the transfer. Lucian (Prom. 4): 'ἡ δὲ ἔφεσις ἐπὶ τὸν Δία ἔσται'. ἐφίεμαι means I desire. The sense: first to try to send forth a dove as an omen, so that it flies, of course, having released it far away from the ship. P
330a. σόη: unharmed. Lg P
b. δίηται: may the bird be pursued and fly. Lg P
332. ἀλλ’ εὖ καρτύναντες: having made secure and strengthened. It is Doric to speak with interchange of letters, as they say κραδίαν and κάρτος.
333-34a. ἐπεὶ φάος οὐ νυ τι τόσσον: the thought is the same as that expressed elsewhere (I 870 sq.):
'οὐδέ τι κῶας αὐτόματον δώσει τις ἑλὼν θεὸς εὐξαμένοισιν.'
b. 〈φάος:〉 life. Sm
335. ὀνήϊστον: most beneficial, you toil and act. He means rowing.
336. πρὶν δ’ οὔτι θεούς: before coming to the strait, I do not prevent you from calling upon the gods as helpers.
341. ὦ μέλεοι: he says this because the heroes were proud of the construction of the Argo, both because of the size of the timbers and the skill of Athena who built it.
